findings.title: Missing authentication on API endpoint
findings.expected: Anonymous requests to protected endpoints return 401 | Authenticated legitimate actor still gets the same 2xx contract
actual: Missing authentication on API endpoint: access was granted
actor anonymous received 200 application/json with the same response contract as positive control S4 (reader_a)
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest> --flows <flows-dir>  (rule NSC-AC-002, flow orders-access step S5)
Open the endpoint in a private browser window: 401/redirect to login
limitations: Evaluated only where a flow declares anonymous `access: denied` with an authenticated positive control; a 2xx with a different contract (login page) is INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL.
findings.recommendation: Apply authentication middleware with deny-by-default to the whole API group; whitelist truly public routes explicitly.
findings.regressionGuard: Public endpoints used before login (health, login config, static config) must be explicitly allow-listed; compare anonymous and authenticated runs before/after.

findings.title: IDOR / BOLA (cross-user object access)
findings.expected: Actor B receives 403/404 for actor A's fixture object | Actor A still receives 200 for its own object (positive control)
actual: IDOR / BOLA (cross-user object access): access was granted
actor reader_b received 200 application/json with the same response contract as positive control S2 (reader_a)
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest> --flows <flows-dir>  (rule NSC-AC-003, flow orders-access step S3)
As actor B in a separate browser profile, paste actor A's object URL: access denied
limitations: UI hiding alone NEVER proves authorization.

Read access: a flow step with object_owner and access: denied. Modification (safe-validate, 0.2.0-c): the same step as a declared fixture mutation, with the owner's own mutation as the positive control.
Whether actor B's change took effect is not compared: NavSentry does not record response body values.
findings.recommendation: Enforce ownership/tenant checks in the service layer for every object lookup; prefer scoped queries (WHERE owner_id = current_user).
findings.regressionGuard: Shared/delegated objects (team, admin, delegated approver) must keep access — encode those rules explicitly and test them as positive controls.

findings.title: Missing function-level authorization (vertical privilege escalation)
findings.expected: Lower role receives 401/403 | Privileged role keeps its 2xx contract (positive control)
actual: Missing function-level authorization (vertical privilege escalation): access was granted
actor reader_a received 200 application/json with the same response contract as positive control S6 (admin)
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest> --flows <flows-dir>  (rule NSC-AC-007, flow orders-access step S7)
As the lower-role user in a separate browser profile, open the privileged URL: access denied
limitations: Hidden menus or disabled buttons never prove authorization.
Evaluated only where a flow declares access: denied for the lower role with a privileged positive control.
findings.recommendation: Enforce deny-by-default role/permission checks on the server for every privileged route or handler; do not rely on hidden menus.
findings.regressionGuard: Delegated or support roles that legitimately use the function must be encoded as positive controls before tightening.

findings.title: National ID / personal identifier disclosure
findings.expected: No checksum-valid national ID / card number appears in responses to actors not entitled to it | Where required for the owner, values are masked (e.g. x-xxxx-xxxxx-12-3)
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-PRIV-001, transport direct-http)
Open the endpoint as an unentitled actor and confirm the field is absent or masked
limitations: SRC-E accepted this as an Exception because the 13-digit value was an internal function identifier, not a citizen ID. NavSentry applies the mod-11 checksum to cut such false positives, but a checksum-valid match is still SUSPECTED until a human confirms the field semantics.
findings.recommendation: Remove or mask the field in the response DTO for unentitled callers; enforce field-level authorization server-side.
findings.regressionGuard: Masking changes values, not keys: keep the field name and type so clients do not break, unless the owner approves removal. Verify JSON shape with `navsentry compare`.

findings.title: Permissive CORS policy
findings.expected: Untrusted test origins are not reflected | Credentials are never allowed with wildcard or reflected origins | Allowed origins are an explicit allowlist
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-AC-004, transport direct-http)
From the legitimate front-end origin the app still works (no CORS errors in Console)
findings.recommendation: Replace origin reflection with an exact-match allowlist; never combine credentials with '*' or 'null'.
findings.regressionGuard: List every legitimate front-end origin (prod, staging, mobile webviews) before tightening; missing one causes CORS errors only in browsers.

findings.title: Content Security Policy missing or unsafe
findings.expected: Every HTML response has an enforcing Content-Security-Policy | script-src (or default-src) contains no 'unsafe-inline' without nonce/hash, no 'unsafe-eval', no '*' | object-src 'none' and base-uri restricted
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-CONF-002, transport direct-http)
Load each main page with DevTools Console open: no CSP violation errors for legitimate functionality
findings.recommendation: Deploy Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first, collect violations from real traffic, refactor inline scripts to nonces/hashes, then switch to the enforcing header.
findings.regressionGuard: An enforcing CSP that is too strict silently breaks scripts, maps, analytics and third-party widgets. Always ship Report-Only first and test every critical page in a real browser. Run `navsentry compare` between the pre-fix and post-fix runs: every legitimate request must keep the same status, content type, non-security header set and JSON shape; only security headers may differ.

findings.title: Cleartext HTTP served without redirect to HTTPS
findings.expected: http:// requests receive 301/308 to the https:// equivalent | No application content or Set-Cookie on http://
actual: Plain HTTP serves content (HTTP 200) without HTTPS redirect
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-CRYPT-006, transport direct-http)
Type http://<host>/ in the browser: it switches to https://
findings.recommendation: Redirect all HTTP to HTTPS at the edge; for internal service ports, enable TLS or restrict them to the internal network.
findings.regressionGuard: Machine clients that POST to http:// may not follow redirects with a body (use 308 to preserve method) — inventory them first.

findings.title: Verbose error, stack trace or unhandled exception exposed
findings.expected: No in-scope response contains stack-trace/exception signatures | Errors return a generic message plus a correlation ID; details go to server logs only | HTTP status codes stay meaningful (4xx for client errors, 5xx for server faults)
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-ERR-001, transport direct-http)
Reproduce the original error condition with a benign request (e.g. missing parameter) and confirm a generic error body
findings.recommendation: Add a global exception handler that logs details server-side and returns a standard error envelope (e.g. RFC 9457 problem+json) without internals; disable framework detailed errors in non-dev environments.
findings.regressionGuard: Keep the SAME status code and the SAME error envelope fields that clients parse (e.g. `success`, `code`, `message`); only remove internal details. Prove it with `navsentry compare` (status + JSON shape must match).

findings.title: JWT missing protection claims or weak algorithm
findings.expected: alg is not 'none' | exp present and lifetime appropriate (e.g. <= 1h for access tokens) | aud and iss present and validated server-side
actual: JWT missing protection claims or weak alg
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-SESS-004, transport direct-http)
Log in, copy the token from DevTools > Network/Storage into a local decoder (offline), check claims
limitations: NavSentry decodes but never verifies or forges tokens.
findings.recommendation: Issue tokens with exp/iat/aud/iss; validate them on every API; reject alg none and unexpected algorithms.
findings.regressionGuard: Adding aud/exp validation rejects old long-lived tokens: plan a token refresh window and communicate client changes.

findings.title: Clickjacking protection missing
findings.expected: HTML responses send CSP frame-ancestors 'self' (or an explicit allowlist) and/or X-Frame-Options DENY|SAMEORIGIN
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-CONF-003, transport direct-http)
From a different local origin, embed the page in an <iframe>: the browser refuses to render it
findings.recommendation: Send `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' <approved-parents>` plus `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` for legacy browsers.
findings.regressionGuard: Inventory legitimate embedding (portals, SSO, map widgets) before choosing DENY. Run `navsentry compare` between the pre-fix and post-fix runs: every legitimate request must keep the same status, content type, non-security header set and JSON shape; only security headers may differ.

findings.title: Unnecessary HTTP methods or method override enabled
findings.expected: OPTIONS on in-scope resources does not advertise TRACE/TRACK/CONNECT | Only methods actually used by the resource are advertised | Method-override headers are ignored (verified manually under safe-validate)
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-CONF-006, transport direct-http)
Send OPTIONS to the resource (NavSentry or curl -X OPTIONS -i) and inspect Allow
limitations: OPTIONS itself being enabled is normal for CORS; SRC-E recorded it as an accepted Exception. NavSentry fails only on dangerous advertised methods.
findings.recommendation: Restrict methods per route at the web server/framework; disable TRACE; remove method-override middleware unless strictly required.
findings.regressionGuard: CORS preflight legitimately needs OPTIONS: do not block OPTIONS globally, only restrict what it advertises. Keep the methods real clients use.

findings.title: Server / framework version disclosure
findings.expected: No response header or default error page exposes a product version number | X-Powered-By / X-AspNet-Version headers removed
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-INFO-001, transport direct-http)
DevTools > Network > Response Headers: no version numbers
limitations: Version hiding is defence in depth, not a fix for an unpatched component (see NSC-SUPPLY-001).
findings.recommendation: Remove/blank version headers at the server/proxy (e.g. server_tokens off, removeServerHeader, enableVersionHeader=false) and use custom error pages.
findings.regressionGuard: Header removal does not change bodies; confirm with `navsentry compare` (Server/X-Powered-By are excluded from the contract).

findings.title: Internal IP address disclosure
findings.expected: No in-scope response contains private IPv4/IPv6 literals in headers or bodies
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-INFO-003, transport direct-http)
Search the raw response (DevTools > Network > Response) for 10./172.16-31./192.168. patterns
limitations: Dotted version/build strings that start with 10. or 192.168. can match; review context before VALIDATED.
findings.recommendation: Stop echoing upstream addresses (Via, X-Backend-Server, error messages, config endpoints); configure the proxy to strip them.
findings.regressionGuard: If a client legitimately consumes an address field (e.g. a config endpoint), replace it with a public hostname rather than removing the field; verify JSON shape with `navsentry compare`.

findings.title: Cookie without HttpOnly flag
findings.expected: Session/auth cookies have HttpOnly | Cookies intentionally read by JS (e.g. double-submit CSRF token) are documented exceptions
actual: SESSIONID: HttpOnly missing on session-like cookie
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-SESS-002, transport direct-http)
DevTools > Application > Cookies: HttpOnly ticked for session cookies
findings.recommendation: Enable HttpOnly for session/auth cookies in the framework configuration.
findings.regressionGuard: Front-end code that reads the cookie will break — search the client code for document.cookie usage first and move it to a header/endpoint.

findings.title: Cookie SameSite missing or contradictory
findings.expected: Session cookies set SameSite=Lax or Strict | Any SameSite=None cookie also has Secure and a documented cross-site need
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-SESS-003, transport direct-http)
DevTools > Application > Cookies: SameSite column
findings.recommendation: Set SameSite=Lax by default; use None; Secure only for cookies that must travel cross-site (SSO, embedded apps).
findings.regressionGuard: SameSite=Strict/Lax can break SAML/OIDC form_post callbacks and payment redirects; test every external login/redirect flow.

findings.title: Email address disclosure
findings.expected: Anonymous responses expose no personal/staff email except intentional public contact addresses listed by the owner
reproduction: navsentry test --config <manifest>  (rule NSC-INFO-004, transport direct-http)
Open the endpoint anonymously and search the response for '@'
limitations: Public contact addresses are expected; record them as reviewed exceptions instead of failing forever.
findings.recommendation: Remove addresses from config/diagnostic endpoints; return them only to authorized users who need them.
findings.regressionGuard: If a UI shows an email field to its owner, keep it for the authenticated owner; remove it only from anonymous/other-user responses.
